The head law is IMPORTED - every candidate comes out of queue_head.head_text and advancing past a blocked row only masks that row's leading marker in a copy of the text, so the line count stays honest and the same law is asked again - and the suite proves the import by patching it (a constant head then reads through as AC-PATCH). PRODUCT: src/os/followup_retry_history.py plus src/os/test_followup_retry_history.py - the house aggregate (followup_history --history) still judged every round from its canonical leg alone, so the four rounds a green retry had repaired were counted red and the aggregate could never read ALL-GREEN (live at R2303: rounds=427 red=412 with four retried rounds). The new reading is one pass over the whole directory whose per-round verdict and leg order are ASKED of followup_retry_legs (a patched joiner moves it - the suite proves it by replacing FR.history), splitting every round into four disjoint classes: green (canonical PASS, last PASS), recovered (canonical not PASS, last PASS), unfixed (canonical not PASS, last not PASS) and regressed (canonical PASS, last not PASS - reported instead of folded into green), with recovered + unfixed PARTITIONING the rounds whose canonical leg is not PASS and a count self-check that refuses E_FRH_COUNT if they ever stop partitioning. A round with no retry leg keeps exactly the followup_history reading (inherited, asserted key by key), and the naming law is asked of retry_naming so an orphan retry leg - invisible to the canonical-only collector - is REFUSED E_FRTL_ORPHAN_RETRY at exit 3 instead of dropping out of the counts. SUITE PASS 6/6 twice with an identical criterion digest, four adjacent followup suites green (retry_legs 6/6, history 7/7, retry_naming 9/9, evidence_variants 6/6), qa/followup-retry-history-R2325.log 1338B as one utf-8 LF single writer through the evidence_capture callable, one runner wiring line (os-followup-retry-history, 6). LIVE ON THE REAL PILE: rounds=438 green=20 retried=6 recovered=5 unfixed=413 regressed=0 verdict=HISTORY-DEBT - and the five recovered rounds are named (R2277, R2289, R2299, R2318, R2320), which is exactly the reading the canonical-only aggregate could never produce. R2807 THE DEFECT AND ITS BIRTH-SITE REPAIR: read_source had no notion of BOM-less UTF-16, so a 40-byte source was accepted as readable text, do_write printed VERDICT PASS over a 41-byte file carrying 20 NUL bytes (a two-line source read back as five lines), and classify() named the result utf-8/lf - the healthy dialect. qa_writer_census.classify_file carries its OWN rule and never asks this tool, so a no-BOM + LF-only + utf-8-decodable file is classified tee and the whole library reads clean: 3106 files under qa/, 155 of them carrying NUL, zero flags. Repaired at the birth site in three places: read_source refuses any source whose DECODED text still holds NUL (endianness cannot be verified without a BOM, so refusal is the honest face), classify names such a file nul-bytes while the BOM checks still run first so the R2775 ps-utf16 class keeps its name and its refusal, and the module docstring states the contract instead of leaving it implied. The same criterion then flipped red to green reading refused=True class=nul-bytes check_rc=2 with a reason that names BOM-less UTF-16.

2026-11-16 R2808 ENGINEERING+CALIBRE CORRECTION: the debt R2807 wrote down in its own hand ("the NUL face was only half repaired") is closed at the birth site, and the first step of closing it was discovering that the debt's own NUMBER was wrong. Three edits in src/os/qa_writer_census.py: CLASSES gains nul-bytes, BASELINE_CLASSES gains it too (so it becomes a known-debt class that can be recorded by name), and classify_file gains `elif b"\x00" in raw -> nul-bytes` placed AFTER the BOM branches and BEFORE the EOL branches - the order is part of the criterion, because the R2775 ps-utf16 name and its refusal must survive. The root cause is stated in the code comment rather than left implied: BOM-less UTF-16 has no BOM to name it, and its every-other-byte NUL padding DECODES AS VALID utf-8, so the crlf==0 branch called it tee - the healthy dialect. A new `nul_bytes=%d` line was added to the --check summary because baselined nul files never flag: without that line the debt would go invisible a second time, which is the whole reason the class exists.

2026-11-18 R2948 PRODUCT+ENGINEERING: the launcher stopped taking its own word for job membership, and the grandson path was finally measured on the SHIPPED panel. Every child is now asked of the KERNEL (IsProcessInJob) after assignment, published per child as job.members/escaped/verified, and a child the kernel says is outside the job makes the launch REFUSE by name instead of being counted as protected. The job also became ANONYMOUS per launcher, because a named job is machine-wide: two launchers were sharing one object, so A's children were members of B's job. The panel gained the other half of the same honesty: it keeps its child's stderr (the only place a named refusal can come from), reports child_exit and child_log in the E_PANEL_NOT_UP body, and stops waiting the moment the child is dead instead of burning the full 25s timeout on a process that already exited 3.
R2948 measured, in order: AC-STL10..AC-STL11 and AC-HSG11 were pinned in src/os/backlog.md BEFORE the code (in-window pre-registration, disclosed). R2950 stopped deleting anything with bytes (a named refusal is the one thing a dead panel cannot replace) and the honest consequence was accumulation: every failed start left a file that nothing on the machine would ever remove. A shipped prune now runs on the CLI panel's own start path and removes a name ONLY when all four of these hold: it is inside bigdomain-panel-child-*.txt, it is older than seven days, its pid does not name a process that could have written it, and the caller did not declare it its own. The liveness half asks the KERNEL, not the name: OpenProcess + GetProcessTimes give the pid's CURRENT holder's creation time, and a process that started AFTER the file was written cannot be its writer - which is the only way a reused pid stops keeping a stale file alive for ever. Every launch prints PANEL-PRUNE removed/kept/fresh/unknown, so the bound is visible instead of claimed.

A decoy outside the namespace and a decoy with a MALFORMED tag are byte-identical after both prunes. 2026-11-19 R2974 PRODUCT+ENGINEERING: a launcher record now names a PROCESS instead of a number. judge() re-measured ALIVENESS but never WHICH process, so a record left behind by a dead launcher kept its pid, the system handed that pid to an unrelated process, and the old record read as a holder again - a dead launcher resurrected by arithmetic. The record now carries pid_started (the creation stamp of the process that wrote it), start_all writes it into both the claim and the serving record, and judge() compares the stamp of the pid CURRENTLY holding that number with the recorded one: an equal stamp means the same process, a different one means the number was recycled and the record is stale for exactly the reason a dead pid is (new reason pid-reused). Two directions are deliberate. A record WITHOUT the field - one an older launcher wrote - is judged exactly as before, so an upgrade never declares a running launcher dead. And a stamp that cannot be MEASURED never demotes a live pid, because judging a real holder stale lets a second launcher take a claim that is really held, which is the worse of the two errors.
